problem_statement: Players Club is a minimalist record-label site built on Astro content collections (artists and albums, album detail pages with cover art and track lists, a homepage artist index, reusable AlbumCard/AlbumGrid components and a shared Header/Footer). Two things are missing. First, the /releases route is still an empty demo stub instead of a real release-drop surface. Second, the label wants a small, consistent 'Now spinning' rail to sit in the footer of every page: a labelled row of the roster's current drops (Neon Dreams, Solar Flare, Electric Velvet, Golden Hour, Velvet Nights) plus a 'Cue next drop' control with a live readout that names which release is currently cued. Ship this so it (1) turns /releases into a complete release-drop page built from the existing album and artist collections (a featured lead drop with cover art, artist, genre, date, release notes and a track list, plus a grid of further releases linking into the album detail routes), (2) renders the shared 'Now spinning' rail in the footer on the home, releases, album and artist pages alike, (3) lays out the rail's chip row responsively without horizontal overflow on a 390px phone, (4) matches Players Club's quiet white/black editorial styling rather than an off-palette slab, and (5) keeps the 'Cue next drop' readout in sync with the control so each click names the newly-cued release. Keep the existing artist/album routing, homepage search/sort/shuffle, the image fade and the Astro build intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Replace the empty /releases demo stub with a complete release-drop page built from the existing albums and artists content collections.
Feature one lead release using its real album cover, artist/stage name, publish date, genre, short Release Notes copy, a Track List, and a link to the album detail page; label it Featured Drop.
Add a grid of several further releases using existing album-cover assets and their real artist relationships, linking into the existing album detail routes.
Add a shared 'Now spinning' rail to the site footer (a shared component invoked from Footer.astro, not a per-page copy) so it renders on the home, releases, album and artist pages.
The rail shows a 'Now spinning' label, a chip row of current drops, and a 'Cue next drop' control with a live readout of the currently-cued release.
The chip row must wrap responsively so no reading surface overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Style the rail in Players Club's quiet white/black editorial language (thin rule, outlined chips keyed to the repo tokens), not an off-palette dark slab.

Wire the 'Cue next drop' readout so that after clicking the control the readout names the newly-cued release in the form 'Cued: <release name>' (e.g. Cued: Solar Flare), reading the live cued chip, never a stale captured value.
Preserve the artist pages, album detail pages, header/footer, homepage search/sort/shuffle, the image fade treatment and the Astro build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Preserve Players Club's minimalist record-label identity: white background, black typography, thin separators, compact bold navigation, square cover art, grayscale secondary text and spare editorial spacing.
Implement the 'Now spinning' rail as a shared component rendered from the single Footer.astro so one source of truth reaches every page; do not paste divergent per-page copies or a detached widget.
The rail's chip row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.
The rail must adopt the repo's own colour tokens and thin-rule idiom so it reads as part of the label, not a foreign block; album covers must stay square and crisp.
The 'Cue next drop' readout must reflect the CURRENT cued release after every click by reading the live cued chip, so it can never go stale relative to the visible selection.
Do not remove or regress the navigation, artist/album routing, homepage controls, image fade or the Astro build.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the rebranded homepage, header nav and responsive shell and carry the 'Now spinning' rail in the footer.

desktop_releases, tablet_releases and mobile_releases are the primary completion states; after the change they show a full release-drop experience (Featured Drop, Track List, Release Notes, Out Now) instead of the demo stub.
desktop_album and desktop_artist verify album/artist routing, cover art, track lists and per-artist album lists remain stable and carry the shared rail in the footer.
desktop_contact verifies simple informational pages still render with the shared BaseLayout/Header/Footer.
desktop_footer_home, mobile_footer_home and desktop_footer_releases scroll the 'Now spinning' rail into view and must show the white/black rail without horizontal overflow.
cue_home clicks the 'Cue next drop' control; the readout must then name the newly-cued release (Solar Flare).

change_completion: The /releases page becomes a complete release-drop surface (Featured Drop lead with cover/artist/genre/date/Release Notes/Track List plus a grid of further releases) rather than a placeholder.
The 'Now spinning' rail is present in the footer of the home, releases, album and artist pages, and after clicking 'Cue next drop' the readout names the newly-cued release.
design_consistency: The rail on the footer states matches the reference's white/black editorial styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-palette slab.
The rail adopts the repo colour tokens and thin-rule idiom; album covers stay square and crisp and paired with the correct album/artist text.
responsive: No captured reading surface overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the rail chip row wraps.
desktop_footer_home, mobile_footer_home and the releases states keep the rail and release grid readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: Navigation, artist pages, album detail pages, the contact page, header/footer and homepage search/sort/shuffle controls remain present and functional.
No broken album/artist links, missing images, raw collection errors or leftover demo-stub copy remain, and the Astro build has no console or network errors.

author_notes: slot_020 L4 hardening of the Players Club Astro music-label site. The release-drop releases page and the shared 'Now spinning' rail component are byte-identical across legs; the L4 levers ride on the rail's footer presence, layout, styling and cue wiring. reference = rail on all pages, fluid wrap, white/black editorial styling keyed to the repo tokens, live cue readout (passes D2/D3/D4/D6). baseline = the original unrepaired rail: present on the home footer only (fails D2 cross-page on releases/album/artist), fixed 760px nowrap chip row (fails D6 mobile overflow ~421px), plain gray slab (fails D3), but its cue readout IS live (passes D4). bad = a 'smart wrong' rail: present on home+releases only (fails D2 album/artist), 560px nowrap + overflow-x:hidden shallow non-fix (fails D6 ~201px), off-palette dark slab (fails D3), and the cue button advances the selection but the readout re-writes a stale captured label (fails D4) — bad fails 4 orthogonal gates. Square album covers and local album-cover image assets ground the release-drop surface; no remote images, fonts or scripts are added.
